findings.title: The unsubscribe link does not mute watched or tracked topics
findings.body: When the current level is `tracking` or `watching`, this branch changes it only to `regular`, which still allows notifications such as replies and mentions. The page says notifications for the topic will stop, but those users can continue receiving them. Set the topic to `muted` for an unsubscribe action.

findings.title: Saving the topic-user row directly bypasses notification-state bookkeeping
findings.body: `TopicUser.change` is needed when changing a notification level: it records `notifications_changed_at` and the user-change reason, and publishes the level change. Saving the row directly leaves those fields unchanged; in particular, a row with a null reason can later be auto-tracked by `update_last_read`, undoing the unsubscribe. Use the shared change method so the preference persists and other clients are notified.

findings.title: A GET request changes the user's notification preference
findings.body: This route exposes `TopicsController#unsubscribe` as GET, and that action writes the user's topic notification level. A cross-site navigation or an email link scanner can therefore trigger the state change without an explicit user confirmation or a CSRF-protected state-changing request. Render a confirmation page on GET and apply the change through a protected POST.

findings.title: The unsubscribe route does not resolve to the added template
findings.body: This declares a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route, which Ember resolves to the `topic-unsubscribe` template name, but the added template is at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (the path for a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route). There is no template-name override, so the unsubscribe page will not render its message and notification control.
